Line 344 hard-codes `timed_out=False` instead of reading the sandbox result, so a Docker/SSH/Colab timeout is stored as not timed out; `good_nodes()` (journal.py:393-398) treats `is_buggy=None` as good, so a node left unevaluated by an exception after append (302-308) is selectable; scoring's `"timed out"` penalty (scoring.py:166-168) is unreachable because a timeout has `returncode` -1 and `runs_ok` False.

Nothing ever creates `origin="debug"` (`_expand_one` only passes `"draft"`/`"improve"`, `_candidate_generator` echoes it, `_execution.py:461-470`), so `_debug_depth` (223) is always 0 and `max_debug_depth` never limits repair of one buggy leaf; `SearchConfig.max_depth` is read nowhere in `search/` (grep), so depth is bounded only by `max_nodes`.

Line 214 averages in the 0.0 confidence of errored critics, so one confident invalid plot plus two critic errors gives 0.33 < 0.6 and `is_verdict_gating` returns None (242), opening the gate; also `_verify_node_plots` does `Path(workdir).rglob` over the shared `runs_dir/"sandbox"` (432-434), so one node is judged on earlier or concurrent nodes' images and a blank one gates later candidates (unverified at runtime, EX-03 blocks it today); `PlotVerdict.is_buggy` and `is_verdict_gating` also answer the same question differently (any-invalid vs confidence-filtered).

Failed runs leave `_experiment_N.py` and every `run_project` leaves `_project_N` forever; the legacy path reads `runs_dir/"sandbox"/"_project"/results.json` (`_execution.py:186-188`) but the sandbox only creates `_project_{counter}` (535), so `structured_results` is never found for the local sandbox; a timed-out experiment's grandchildren survive (child-only kill).

`run()` does `staging.mkdir(exist_ok=True)` (220) with no stale clear, unlike `run_project` (244-245), and the per-instance counter restarts at 1 for each factory-built sandbox, so two concurrent instances on one workdir share `_docker_run_1` and the first `finally: rmtree` (232) deletes the other's staging mid-run; an infrastructure failure returns `returncode=-1` "Docker execution error" (428-434) indistinguishable from an experiment crash (see EX-12).

On `TimeoutExpired` only the local ssh client dies (393-405); the remote process (or un-named docker container, 324-371) keeps running and `rm -rf` (278) removes its working dir under it; failed `rm` (15 s, result ignored) leaks the remote dir; `_ssh_run_N` local staging accumulates and a fresh instance reuses `_ssh_run_1` with stale files that `scp -r` (427) uploads.

`shutil.copytree` into `pending/` (329) is not atomic and there is no ready marker, so the worker's 10 s poll can rename a half-copied task to `running/` and run it without `main.py`; on timeout only `pending/` is handled (345), so a task already in `running/` finishes later into `done/` and is never collected, and the unguarded `rmtree` (346) can raise if the worker renames between `exists()` and `rmtree` (timing unverified); `effective_timeout = max(timeout_sec, config.timeout_sec)` (334) overrides a shorter caller timeout.

Infrastructure failures (Docker daemon error 428, SSH mkdir/scp failure ssh_sandbox 222,234, Drive read error colab 386) are `returncode=-1` with no flag, so they read as the experiment's own `"failed"`; the stage still returns `StageStatus.DONE` for `"failed"`/`"rejected"` (`_execution.py:391-394`, pipeline cluster to confirm).

`current_code = next_code` (200) runs even when the result was discarded, so the next LLM improvement starts from the discarded code, not from the kept best; `improved` and `kept` diverge (`kept` needs delta > `keep_threshold`) and the stop counter uses `improved` (216), not `kept`.

`run_loop` returns early at runner.py:194 (`llm is None`) before `return_to_original_branch` (227) and has no `finally`, so an exception or the early return leaves the user's repo on `experiment/<tag>`; `discard_experiment` runs `git reset --hard HEAD` (57) and `commit_experiment` `git add -A` (36), destroying or committing unrelated uncommitted user changes.

`_initialize_workers` appends to `self._workers` without clearing (248), so `create_pool` (456) followed by `execute_parallel` (200), or a second `execute_parallel`, doubles the workers, duplicates `worker-N` ids in `_status`, and pushes workers past the semaphore list (290); `_running` is not reset if `queue.join()` raises (218-221), leaving "Pool is already running" (193-194); the outer `except TimeoutError` (302) is dead because `_execute_with_timeout` catches it (380).

`isolation.execute` returns only stdout (isolation.py:250,424,558), so a non-zero exit, Docker error or sandbox timeout still yields `ExperimentResult(kept=True, error=None, stderr="")` (150-162); `config.timeout` (145) ignores the pool's `timeout_per_experiment`.

`WorktreeIsolation.cleanup` computes the branch name and discards it (436) and runs `worktree remove` without `--force`, which fails on the untracked `experiment.py` (403-404), so the worktree and branch `exp-<id>` leak and a re-run of the same design id fails at `git worktree add -b` (343-352); on timeout `wait_for(proc.communicate())` (242,416) never kills the process or container (no `--name`).

A survey/selection failure returns a default `BenchmarkPlan` (240-245, 261-266) with empty lists and `validation_passed=False` and no failure marker, indistinguishable from "nothing found"; failure paths skip `benchmark_plan.json` (346); whether the consumer distinguishes them is unverified.

When the critic call fails (`success` False, `reviews` empty) `critic_feedback` is `[]`, `failed_ids` empty and `figures` becomes `[]` (458-461): the loop stops retrying on nothing and returns unreviewed figures; the return value is `final_rendered` with no per-figure `passed` flag, so figures that never passed review at `max_iterations` look final.

`_chat_json` returns `{}` on unparseable output (base.py:111), so `quality_score` defaults to 5 with no issues (critic.py:355) and the visual-quality dimension passes as if reviewed; a raised LLM error instead fails the whole critic (124-126, see EX-20).
